messages:
Anita P.: quick sync — thinking about the fallback trigger surface. we have latency SLOs (p50 < 80ms, p99 < 400ms) and quality guardrails (eval score drop > 3%). how should we combine these into a single decision policy?

Jae K.: currently runtime uses simple rule: if latency breach => immediate fallback. that keeps p99 but sometimes pulls high-quality variants too early. want a hybrid.

Ben R.: +1. what about a weighted scoring function that normalizes latency breach and quality drift into a single score, then compare to a threshold? lightweight, tunable per-route.

Anita P.: can you sketch a pseudo-policy?

Marco L.: sure, here's a minimal example we used in the prototype:

```json
{
  "policy_type": "hybrid_score",
  "weights": {"latency": 0.6, "quality": 0.4},
  "latency_window": "1m",
  "quality_window": "10m",
  "score_threshold": 0.7,
  "min_samples": 100
}
```

Priya S.: tradeoffs: weights need per-tenant/workload tuning. also important: action semantics — soft degrade (route to cheaper/quantized variant) vs hard fallback (baseline model). and hysteresis (avoid flip-flopping).

Anita P.: agreed. hysteresis idea: require N consecutive score breaches OR sustained average > threshold for T seconds, plus a cool_down after fallback. otherwise we get oscillation.

eng-observer-bot: observer: probe report @ 2026-02-05T11:32:10Z — model=redwood-7b region=us-west p99_latency=820ms (SLO breach), eval_drift=+5.2% on promptset=search_short, sample_count=240.

Jae K.: nice. ok that points to a real event where latency and quality both moved. question: where should the decision live? runtime needs low-latency actions; control plane has richer evals and longer windows.

Ben R.: propose split responsibility: runtime enforces fast-latency hedges (eg. switch to cached response, lower batch sizes, or immediate fallback to pre-warmed variant) using short windows (1m). control plane runs the hybrid scoring on longer windows (5–15m) and issues rollout policy updates (change weight/threshold or pin variant). runtime subscribes to control-plane decisions.

Marco L.: that matches our reliability constraints: runtime must be able to do an emergency fallback with <500ms decision path. control-plane handles stable policy changes and telemetry synthesis.

Priya S.: also need safety nets: 1) require a minimum sample volume before an automatic fallback (avoid noisy small-sample flips), 2) preserve monotonic rollback: once we fallback to baseline, require a canary warmup before re-escalation.

Anita P.: implementation details: add fields to the policy contract: `min_samples`, `cool_down_s`, `recovery_samples`, `action_priority` (soft->hard). runtime will implement a simplified evaluator with same weight/threshold semantics. control plane runs the canonical evaluator and can override weights per-tenant.

Marco L.: example action enum we discussed: `actions = ["graceful-degrade", "route-to-baseline", "drain-canary", "block-new-variants"]`. runtime picks the highest-priority allowed action.

Ben R.: monitoring: we should emit a single decision event with metadata: {policy_id, score, components:{latency,quality}, samples, action, decision_ts}. that makes audits and postmortems easy.

eng-observer-bot: note: scheduled evaluator will emit `decision_event` when control-plane hybrid score crosses threshold. sample payload will include `policy_id` and `raw_metrics`.

Jae K.: ops/alerts: we want two alerts — a P0 for unexpected hard fallbacks (route-to-baseline happened without a matching control-plane decision) and a P1 for repeated soft-degrades.

Priya S.: testing: add a simulated harness that runs synthetic latency spikes + targeted quality perturbations per-route to validate both hysteresis and recovery logic. include tests for partial signals (latency-only, quality-only, both).

Anita P.: plan of record: 1) Marco to land policy schema PR with supporting fields (weights, min_samples, cool_down, action_priority) — due EOD Tue. 2) Ben to add decision_event telemetry and alert hooks — due Thu. 3) Jae to wire runtime fast-path for graceful-degrade and route-to-baseline — due next Tue. 4) Priya to add sim tests and canary scenario set — due next Fri.

Ben R.: acked. I'll also add a small CLI to dump current policy evaluation for a route: `redwoodctl policy eval --route X --window 60s` for debug.

Marco L.: one more thought: keep defaults conservative (favor quality) and expose per-route overrides for latency-sensitive flows.

Anita P.: perfect. follow-up: @Jae K. can you add a short blurb in the runtime README about the emergency fallback code path and the expected decision latency? will help oncall.

Jae K.: will do.

Priya S.: thanks everyone — I'll start drafting the sim tests and share a small promptset for the quality probes. :wave:
